summary: @umschool/analytics postinstall exfiltrates host info and parent project source to attacker-controlled request-catcher
details: The package is a dependency-confusion lure: a scoped name (@umschool/analytics) published at an implausibly high version (999.0.3) with empty index.js stubs, whose only functional code is a postinstall script. On npm install, postinstall.js collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo(), process.cwd(), /etc/hostname, /proc/version, and selected process.env values, walks upward from the install directory to locate the parent project's app.js/index.js/server.js/main.js, reads up to 2 KB of that file, base64-encodes the payload, and exfiltrates it as an HTTPS GET query parameter to akko.requestcatcher.com. A parallel DNS channel encodes hostname and username into subdomain labels of the same host. The behavior fires automatically on install without any user invocation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
